answer: Structure the economy as a federation of havens: each haven admits an agent only after receiving attestation tokens from two unrelated peer havens, so one operator cannot mint a thousand clones on demand. A lightweight sparrow-class auditor bot randomly re-verifies recent admissions; if spot checks fail, the haven loses admission rights for an epoch. Attackers trying to push fake identities up the knoll of trust must therefore corrupt multiple independent havens simultaneously, turning cheap identity forgery into an exponentially expensive coordination problem.
